newsitem.title: CHINA: HK business heads say confident, proud of new era.
newsitem.headline: HK business heads say confident, proud of new era.

text.p: Top business executives in Hong Kong expressed confidence and pride in the new Hong Kong on Tuesday after attending ceremonies to mark the territory's handover from Britain to China.
"I feel proud when I see the five-star flag (of China) go up. It is a happy day for the Chinese," said Richard Li Tzar Kai, son of Cheung Kong chairman Li Ka Shing.
Several thousand guests saw the flags of Britain and colonial Hong Kong lowered and the flags of China and the Special Administrative Region of Hong Kong raised.
Hong Kong reverted to Chinese rule at midnight June 30 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
Stanley Ho, chairman of Shun Tak Holdings, said he was impressed by the speech of China's President Jiang Zemin.
"Jiang made a very good speech, with his assurances that Hong Kong will retain its capitalist system for 50 years," said Ho.
Ho also said he believed that Hong Kong would remain a good place to do business and predicted that the stock exchange would continue to rise.
David Law Smith, chairman of the board and chief executive officer at Caltex Petroleum Corp, said the ceremony was "impressive and nostalgic".
"It's impressive because Hong Kong has an influence on the change in China. In our view, the success of China will permiate the whole Chinese system over time," said Smith.
Elizabeth Wong, a legislator in the British era, said she believed the ceremony was a good sign that the British and Chinese are good friends.
Wong also said she believed Jiang was sincere in his promise to implement a "one country, two systems" formula for Hong Kong's autonomy.
Many people attending the late-night ceremony appeared emotionally drained and tired after days of festivities to mark the handover. But Wong said she remained stoic during the proceedings.
"I didn't cry at the ceremony. I am a strong woman," she said.
